extracted.intended_audience: self-published / indie authors seeking a Kirkus Traditional Review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and service description for Kirkus Indie Traditional Reviews: a pre-publication, professionally written ~250–350-word review that summarizes a book for context and gives a concise, unbiased opinion, with options to publish the review on Kirkus platforms or keep it private.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review length
rubrics_metrics.description: About 250-300 words, our reviews include summary to give our readers context, along with a concise, unbiased opinion... (page also states reviewers will write a full review approximately 250-350 words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are short-form, roughly a few hundred words (page text gives both 'about 250-300 words' and 'approximately 250-350 words'); expect a single concise review rather than long-form coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include summary to give readers context
rubrics_metrics.description: Our reviews include summary to give our readers context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review should briefly summarize the book so readers understand premise, scope, or plot as necessary to interpret the critic's opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise, unbiased opinion (positive/negative/mixed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Along with a concise, unbiased opinion that can be positive, negative, or, most likely, mixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critique should be impartial and succinct; it may praise or fault the book or strike a balanced/mixed tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give both general worth and specific strengths/weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Kirkus review gives both a general sense of a book’s worth and specific information about its strengths and weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review should state an overall evaluation (worth/merit) while citing concrete examples or areas where the book succeeds or fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer reads the complete book
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of your book or manuscript, our editor will assign your project to a qualified reviewer who will read the complete book and write a full review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are based on a full reading of the manuscript rather than excerpted sections; expect a thorough read before the critic forms their evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer qualifications / professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Our reviewers include librarians, business executives, journalists from national publications, PhDs in religion and literature, creative executives in entertainment and publishing industries as well as other professional reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kirkus uses experienced, professional reviewers from a range of relevant backgrounds to ensure informed criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: How reviewers are chosen (editor analysis and matching)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Kirkus editor analyzes your book and considers its elements individually, including content, style, and voice. The editor matches your book with a reviewer who has significant experience with and appreciates your book’s genre and topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key elements weighed in matching include content, style, voice, genre, and topical expertise; matching aims to align reviewer experience with the book's subject/genre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and delivery process
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process: 1) Request review (select Traditional Review). 2) Submit manuscript (follow instructions to send book). 3) Stand by while we review your book. 4) Download review (link emailed to author dashboard). 5) Keep your review private or publish it on KirkusReviews.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must submit the book after ordering; Kirkus emails confirmations and the final review via the author dashboard. Publishing the review on Kirkus sites is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to keep review private or publish
rubrics_metrics.description: After you read your review, you will have the option to publish it on KirkusReviews.com... You may keep your review private by simply not publishing it on our site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors control whether the review is made public; publishing increases discoverability by industry influencers, agents, publishers, and consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of published reviews (marketing and industry visibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish it on KirkusReviews.com, where it may be discovered by industry influencers, agents, publishers, and consumers. Our editors will also consider your review for publication in Kirkus Reviews magazine...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published Kirkus reviews can be used as marketing collateral or to attract agent/publisher attention; publication in the magazine is selective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kirkus Star designation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kirkus Star marks books of exceptional merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Star is a curated designation indicating exceptional quality; the page states it is 'one of the most coveted designations in the book industry' though no specific awarding criteria are listed here.
